qc.label_under_test: In practical how-to text (web forms, documents, medicines), the 'and' / 'and then' that adds a second step after a first action, and that second step's verb (e.g. 'register online and then print'); any person or tense. Plain 'you can also...' offers and single-step instructions stay low.

neighbours.label: In step-by-step instructions addressed to the reader (web forms, documents, medicines), the 'and' / 'and then' that chains a second action after a first, and that next step's verb (e.g. 'register online and then print'); the same chain told as a story or past-tense narration stays low.
fire: To apply, register online and then print your confirmation page.
Fill in your name and address, and then click Submit at the bottom of the form.
Shake the bottle well and take two tablets with a full glass of water.
Open the attached document, sign the last page and return it by Friday.
Enter your password twice and then select a security question.
Remove the protective seal and insert the inhaler into the spacer.
Download the template, and then save a copy to your own drive before editing.
Dissolve one sachet in warm water and drink immediately after meals.
quiet: Last week she registered online and then printed her confirmation page.
He filled in his name and address, and then clicked Submit at the bottom of the form.
My grandfather shook the bottle well and took two tablets with a full glass of water.
She opened the attached document, signed the last page and returned it by Friday.
I entered my password twice and then selected a security question.
The nurse removed the protective seal and inserted the inhaler into the spacer.

predictions: Expect the narrow instruction-vs-story contrast to be only partly clean: the pole is diffuse (solver max 0.39), so I expect about 5/8 fire sentences above 0.20 and 1-3 narrative near misses to leak. Likely fail on AUROC.
